chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A hairdresser entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he said to her, 'Have you abandoned your work or do you continue in it?' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I do it unless you forbid me from it, so I will cease from it.' He said, 'Do it. So when you comb, do not scratch the face with porcelain, for it removes the moisture of the face, and do not join hair to hair.'

key_terms.اَلْخَزَفِ: Porcelain or ceramic (used here for scratching/combing)
key_terms.مَاءِ اَلْوَجْهِ: Moisture of the face (natural oils/skin health)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to a female hairdresser regarding her profession and specific grooming practices?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of professions, this hadith illustrates the Prophet’s pragmatic approach to women’s economic participation, affirming that grooming services are permissible unless explicitly prohibited. The specific instructions regarding avoiding harsh facial scrubbing with porcelain (*khazzaf*) and hair extension highlight a balance between aesthetic enhancement and preserving natural beauty, reflecting early Shia jurisprudence on modesty and professional ethics in domestic trades.
